claims.text: For \((r,q,i,j)=(2,6,1,1)\) and \((5,2,1,1)\), one has \(a=b=1\), hence \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}=2\). The two prescribed families specialize respectively to \(\{s_{(1)},s_{(2)}\}\) and \(\{s_{(1)},s_{(1,1)}\}\).

In the standard integral Grassmannian quotient \(A\) for either \(2^6\) or \(6^2\), \(A\) is generated by \(h_1,h_2\), and \[ A_+=(h_1,h_2),\qquad A_+/A_+^2\cong\mathbb Z\bar h_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar h_2. \] Indeed, for \(q=2\), \(h_k=0\) for \(k>2\). For \(r=2\), \(e_k=0\) for \(k>2\), so \(h_m=e_1h_{m-1}-e_2h_{m-2}\), with \(e_1=h_1\) and \(e_2=h_1^2-h_2\). In degree \(2\), \(A_2\) has basis \(s_{(2)},s_{(1,1)}\), while \((A_+^2)_2=\mathbb Z(s_{(2)}+s_{(1,1)})\).

Assuming the Theorem-5.4 generation assertion for these specialized families, both displayed two-element sets are minimal generating sets for \(J_{v_{2,2,2,8}}\) and \(J_{v_{5,5,5,7}}\). The first set is \(\{h_1,h_2\}\), hence generates \(A_+\) and therefore \(J_v=A_+\). The second is \(\{h_1,e_2\}\), and \(e_2=h_1^2-h_2\), so it generates the same ideal. Modulo \(A_+^2\), its images are \((\bar h_1,-\bar h_2)\); thus each pair is a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(J_v/A_+J_v\), so neither member is deletable.
